Densities of particles on 𝐑 n {{\mathbf{R}}^{n}} which interact pairwise through an attractive-repulsive power-law potential W α , β ​ ( x ) = | x | α / α − | x | β / β W_{\alpha,\beta}(x)=|x|^{\alpha}/\alpha-|x|^{\beta}/\beta have often been used to explain patterns produced by biological and physical systems.

Thanks: Seungryong Kim is with the Department of Computer Sc
arxiv-2201-01883.creator: Jaehoon Cho, Seungryong Kim
arxiv-2201-01883.description: Abstract This paper addresses the problem of single image de-raining, that is, the task of recovering clean and rain-free background scenes from a single image obscured by a rainy artifact. Although recent advances adopt real-world time-lapse data to overcome the need for paired rain-clean images, they are limited to fully exploit the time-lapse data.

arxiv-2202-13384.title: From sub-aging to hyper-aging in structural glasses
arxiv-2202-13384.creator: Luis F. Elizondo-Aguilera, Tommaso Rizzo, Thomas Voigtmann
arxiv-2202-13384.description: A 2022 arXiv research paper by Luis F. Elizondo-Aguilera, Tommaso Rizzo, Thomas Voigtmann. We demonstrate non-equilibrium scaling laws for the aging dynamics in glass formers that emerge from combining a recent application of Onsager’s theory of irreversible processes with the equilibrium scaling laws of glassy dynamics.

arxiv-2402-14321.title: Non-relativistic spin splitting in compensated magnets that are not altermagnets
arxiv-2402-14321.creator: Lin-Ding Yuan, Alexandru B. Georgescu, James M. Rondinelli
arxiv-2402-14321.description: A 2024 arXiv research paper by Lin-Ding Yuan, Alexandru B. Georgescu, James M. Rondinelli. The non-relativistic spin-splitting (NRSS) of electronic bands in “altermagnets” has sparked renewed interest in antiferromagnets (AFMs) that have no net magnetization. However, altermagnets with collinear and compensated magnetism are not the only type of NRSS AFMs. In this study, we identify the symmetry conditions and characteristic signatures of a distinct group of NRSS AFMs that go beyond the description of altermagnets.

arxiv-2405-03713.title: Improve Cross-Modality Segmentation by Treating T1-weighted MRI Images as Inverted CT Scans
arxiv-2405-03713.creator: Hartmut Häntze, Lina Xu, Maximilian Rattunde, Leonhard Donle, Felix J. Dorfner, Alessa Hering, Lisa C. Adams, Keno K. Bressem ‡ \ddagger
arxiv-2405-03713.description: Abstract Computed tomography (CT) segmentation models often contain classes that are not currently supported by magnetic resonance imaging (MRI) segmentation models. In this study, we show that a simple image inversion technique can significantly improve the segmentation quality of CT segmentation models on MRI data.

arxiv-2405-04187.title: Self-Similar Properties of the Proton Structure at Low x within the xFitter framework
arxiv-2405-04187.creator: Shahin Atashbar Tehrani 1,2 ID, Fatemeh Taghavi-Shahri 3 ID, Samira Shoeibi Mohsenabadi 3 ID
arxiv-2405-04187.description: Abstract The structure of the proton exhibits Fractal behavior at low x , where x is the fraction of the proton’s momentum carried by the interacting partons. This Fractal behavior is characterized by self-similar properties at different scales and can be quantified using the concept of Fractal dimension.

arxiv-2509-15621.title: Concept Unlearning in Large Language Models via Self-Constructed Knowledge Triplets
arxiv-2509-15621.creator: Tomoya Yamashita, Yuuki Yamanaka, Masanori Yamada, Takayuki Miura, Toshiki Shibahara, Tomoharu Iwata
arxiv-2509-15621.description: Abstract Machine Unlearning (MU) has recently attracted considerable attention as a solution to privacy and copyright issues in large language models (LLMs). Existing MU methods aim to remove specific target sentences from an LLM while minimizing damage to unrelated knowledge. However, these approaches require explicit target sentences and do not support removing broader concepts, such as persons or events.

arxiv-2601-17871.title: A Physics-Informed Digital Twin Framework for Calibrated Sim-to-Real FMCW Radar Occupancy Estimation
arxiv-2601-17871.creator: Huy Trinh, Sebastian Ratto V, Elliot Creager, George Shaker
arxiv-2601-17871.description: Abstract Learning robust radar perception models directly from real measurements is costly due to the need for controlled experiments, repeated calibration, and extensive annotation. This paper proposes a lightweight simulation-to-real (sim2real) framework that can enable reliable Frequency Modulated Continuous Wave (FMCW) radar occupancy detection and people counting using only a physics-informed geometric simulator plus a small unlabeled real calibration set.

pmc-10555176.title: OR13-04 Risk Of Wrist Fracture In Gastric Bypass Compared To Gastric Banding As Estimated By The Load-To-Strength Ratio
pmc-10555176.creator: Grace H Jung, Bita Zahedi, Katherine Lindeman, Claire C Rushin, Michael C Cheney, Mary L Bouxsein, Elaine Wei-Yin Yu
pmc-10555176.description: A peer-reviewed research article from Europe PMC (2023). Yu: Grant Recipient; Self; Amgen Inc. Background: Bariatric surgeries such as Roux-en-Y gastric bypass (RYGB) and adjustable gastric banding (AGB) lead to long-term deficits in bone density but are also accompanied by decreased weight, which may lower the impact force with falls. Given that risk of fracture is dependent on both bone strength and the external force applied to bone, the clinical implications of these opposing effects are unclear.

pmc-10648881.title: Graph Neural Networks for Parkinson’s Disease Monitoring and Alerting
pmc-10648881.creator: Nikolaos Zafeiropoulos, Pavlos Bitilis, George E Tsekouras, Konstantinos Kotis, Yu-Dong Zhang
pmc-10648881.description: Graph neural networks (GNNs) have been increasingly employed in the field of Parkinson’s disease (PD) research. The use of GNNs provides a promising approach to address the complex relationship between various clinical and non-clinical factors that contribute to the progression of PD.

pmc-10650695.title: Guided Direct Time-of-Flight Lidar Using Stereo Cameras for Enhanced Laser Power Efficiency
pmc-10650695.creator: Filip Taneski, Istvan Gyongy, Tarek Al Abbas, Robert K Henderson, Ruben Pauwels
pmc-10650695.description: A peer-reviewed research article from Europe PMC (2023). Self-driving vehicles demand efficient and reliable depth-sensing technologies. Lidar, with its capability for long-distance, high-precision measurement, is a crucial component in this pursuit. However, conventional mechanical scanning implementations suffer from reliability, cost, and frame rate limitations. Solid-state lidar solutions have emerged as a promising alternative, but the vast amount of photon data processed and stored using conventional direct time-of-flight (dToF) prevents long-distance sensing unless power-intensive partial histogram approaches are used.

pmc-10669237.title: Ascorbate Uptake and Retention by Breast Cancer Cell Lines and the Intracellular Distribution of Sodium-Dependent Vitamin C Transporter 2
pmc-10669237.creator: Citra Praditi, Stephanie M. Bozonet, Gabi U. Dachs, Margreet C. M. Vissers
pmc-10669237.description: Ascorbate plays a vital role as a co-factor for a superfamily of enzymes, the 2-oxoglutarate dependent dioxygenases (2-OGDDs), which govern numerous pathways in cancer progression, including the hypoxic response and the epigenetic regulation of gene transcription. Ascorbate uptake into most cells is through active transport by the sodium-dependent vitamin C transporter 2 (SVCT2).

pmc-11577216.title: Comparative transcriptomic analysis revealed potential mechanisms regulating the hypertrophy of goose pectoral muscles
pmc-11577216.creator: Xinyue Hu, Yali Liu, Bincheng Tang, Jiwei Hu, Hua He, Hehe Liu, Liang Li, Shenqiang Hu, Jiwen Wang
pmc-11577216.description: Pectoral muscle development is an important economic trait. According to the different essence, muscle development can be divided into 2 processes: embryonic muscle fiber generation and postnatal muscle fiber hypertrophy, and postnatal muscle fiber hypertrophy has a greater impact on muscle development than the number of muscle fibers formed during the embryonic phase in poultry.

pmc-11602257.title: Comparison of the predicted and achieved labiolingual inclinations of the maxillary central incisors in adult Class II division 2 malocclusions treated with clear aligners
pmc-11602257.creator: Mariam Al-Samman, Mais Sadek, Ahmad M. Hamdan
pmc-11602257.description: ObjectiveThis study aimed to compare the predicted and achieved labiolingual inclinations of the maxillary central incisors in adult Class II division 2 malocclusions treated with clear aligners using Power Ridges® and composite attachments.MethodsThis retrospective study included 24 patients (mean age, 26.5 ± 3.3 years).

pmc-11645115.title: Prevalence and determinants of double and triple burden of malnutrition among mother–child pairs in Malawi: a mapping and multilevel modelling study
pmc-11645115.creator: Jessie Jane Khaki, Peter M Macharia, Lenka Beňová, Emanuele Giorgi, Aline Semaan
pmc-11645115.description: Objective:To establish the prevalence of double burden of malnutrition (DBM) and triple burden of malnutrition (TBM) among mother–child pairs in Malawi and explore their geographical distribution and associated multilevel factors.Design:Cross-sectional study using secondary data from the 2015–2016 Malawi Demographic and Health Survey using a mixed effects binomial model to identify multilevel factors associated with DBM and TBM.

pmc-11710907.title: Prevalence of Programmed Death-Ligand 1 Positivity Using SP142 in Patients With Advanced Stage Triple-Negative Breast Cancer in Malaysia: A Cross-Sectional Study
pmc-11710907.creator: Pathmanathan Rajadurai, Ning Yi Yap, Seow Fan Chiew, Reena Rahayu Md Zin, Suria Hayati Md Pauzi, Aniqah Shamimi Binti Jaafar, Azyani Yahaya, Lai Meng Looi
pmc-11710907.description: PurposeTriple-negative breast cancer (TNBC) is a subtype of breast cancer known for its poor prognosis and the absence of viable targets for standard receptor-based therapies. Several studies have suggested that targeting programmed death-ligand 1 (PD-L1) in tumors that express this biomarker, either on tumor cells and/or in the tumor inflammatory infiltrate, may be beneficial in some patients.

pmc-12663501.title: Quality attributes, metabolomics and microbial community dynamics of naturally fermented Xiaohuang ginger (Zingiber officinale cv. Xiaohuang): A ready-to-eat flavoring food
pmc-12663501.creator: Jiajia Wang, Hongru He, Lianbing Lin, Yicen Lin, Feng Wang
pmc-12663501.description: A peer-reviewed research article from Europe PMC (2025). Ginger, a popular dietary condiment, is rarely consumed directly due to its intense pungency. Pickled Xiaohuang ginger, a ready-to-eat flavoring food, has become prevalent in Southwest China, yet its quality traits, metabolite profiles, and microbial dynamics remain largely unexplored. In this study, we extensively examined the physicochemical properties, flavor characteristics, metabolome, and microbial dynamics (encompassing both bacterial and fungal communities) during a 42-day natural fermentation of Xiaohuang ginger.

pmc-13520265.creator: Corné Nel, Jacqueline E Wolvaardt, Pieter du Toit

pmc-13544498.title: Determining the Minimal Clinically Important Difference of the 40‐Item Smell Identification Test in People With Cystic Fibrosis
pmc-13544498.creator: Eugene Oh, Jessa E. Miller, Michelle J. Lee, Anna Zemke, David Baraghoshi, Matthew J. Strand, Jeremiah A. Alt, Todd E. Bodner, Michael Chang, Naweed I. Chowdhury, Patricia H. Eshaghian, Anne E. Getz, Jennifer L. Goralski, David A. Gudis, Peter H. Hwang, Ashoke Khanwalkar, Adam J. Kimple, Jivianne T.
pmc-13544498.description: BackgroundChronic rhinosinusitis (CRS) and olfactory dysfunction (OD) are highly prevalent among people with cystic fibrosis (PwCF) and negatively impact quality of life. The 40‐item Smell Identification Test (SIT) is widely used to assess psychophysical olfaction, but a CF‐specific minimal clinically important difference (MCID) has not been established.

pmc-13675921.title: Mouse models to study von Willebrand factor in thrombosis: a scoping review
pmc-13675921.creator: Veronica DeYoung, Hassan Masood, Peter Andrisani, Arthane Kodeeswaran, Taylor Sparring, Jaskirat Arora, Natasha Savic, Jonathan L. Babulic, Patricia C. Liaw, Davide Matino, Alison Fox-Robichaud, Colin A. Kretz
pmc-13675921.description: A peer-reviewed research article from Europe PMC (2026). Backgroundvon Willebrand factor (VWF) plays a significant role in blood coagulation and inflammation and is a key driver of many thrombotic conditions. Identifying appropriate mouse models is critical to developing effective and safe VWF-targeted therapies.ObjectivesThis scoping review aims to identify and evaluate all mouse models of thrombosis that have demonstrated functional involvement of VWF and/or its primary regulator, ADAMTS-13, followed by a critical review of common models.MethodsA comprehensive literature search was conducted to identify studies published from database inception to October 2024
